one_liner: Makes information look right and read clearly - logos, packaging, posters, brand systems.
job_roles: Graphic Designer | Brand Identity Designer | Packaging Designer | Layout & Publication Designer | Motion Graphics Designer | Signage & Wayfinding Designer | Social Media Creative Designer | Typographer
self_emp_route: Freelance and small-studio work built off the same portfolio used to get hired; a one-person studio serving local businesses is the commonest form.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. Generative image tools now produce competent layouts, social creatives and packaging mockups from a prompt, and that is exactly the entry-level work a junior is hired to do. Social Media Creative Designer and Layout & Publication Designer face this first. Brand Identity Designer is the protected end - the work there is deciding what a company should look like and defending the call to people who disagree, which is clarity, not output.
role_spread: [Motion Graphics Designer] higher: spatial, logical / lower: verbal || [Brand Identity Designer] higher: verbal, openness, confidence / lower: attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. No subject is required. -> training: A 1-2 year diploma in graphic or communication design, or a B.Des. Neither is legally required. -> portfolio: Build a portfolio of 10-15 real pieces. This, not the certificate, is what gets read at hiring. -> work: Junior designer at a studio, agency or in-house brand team; or freelance from the portfolio directly.
nuances: [degree_dependency] There is no qualification here at all. The portfolio IS the credential, and a self-taught designer with good work competes directly with a B.Des graduate. That cuts both ways: entry is genuinely open, and nothing protects the practitioner from being undercut. || [ai_exposure] The bottom rung is shrinking, not the profession. Studios still need someone to decide what is right and take responsibility for it - what they need fewer of is people to produce the twentieth variation of a banner.

one_liner: Designs how an app or website works and feels, so people can use it without being taught.
job_roles: UX Designer | UI Designer | Interaction Designer | UX Researcher | Design Systems Designer | Information Architect | Usability Analyst | Service Designer | Product Designer (Digital)
self_emp_route: Freelance product design for startups, or a small independent studio. Common after 4-6 years, once a case-study portfolio can win work on its own.
ai_reason: Screens generate easily; understanding does not. UI Designer is the exposed role - tools already produce clean, conventional layouts from a description. UX Researcher and Service Designer are the protected end, for the same reason an IT Business Analyst is: the work is establishing what a room of people who disagree actually need, and a model cannot know whose problem it is.
role_spread: [UX Researcher, Usability Analyst] higher: verbal, emotional_intelligence, reasoning / lower: spatial || [Design Systems Designer] higher: conscientiousness, logical, attention_span / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Des, or any bachelor's degree followed by a UX course. Psychology, English and engineering graduates all enter this way. -> portfolio: Three or four case studies showing a problem, the research, the decisions and the outcome - not just screens. -> work: Junior UX or UI designer on a product team.
nuances: [industrial_sectors] Routed here from Sector 1. The tools are digital and the employer is usually a software company, but the object of concern is the person using the product - swap the software out for a hospital form or an ATM and the work survives unchanged. || [entry_competition] Null on purpose. This is one of the few well-paid Indian professions with no gate of any kind - no exam, no licence, no required degree subject. A commerce or arts graduate can enter it directly, which is rare in this dataset.

one_liner: Makes drawings and digital models move - for film, series, games and advertising.
job_roles: 2D Animator | 3D Animator | Character Rigger | VFX Compositor | Modelling & Texturing Artist | Lighting & Rendering Artist | Storyboard Artist | Matchmove Artist | Roto & Paint Artist | Motion Capture Artist
self_emp_route: Freelance shots and sequences for studios, which is how a large part of the industry already works; established artists take contract work directly from overseas clients.
ai_reason: Generative video and automated rotoscoping attack this profession from the bottom, which is the worst place to be attacked. Roto & Paint Artist and Matchmove Artist are the exposed roles, and they are precisely the rungs India's outsourced VFX industry hires at volume. Character Rigger, Lighting & Rendering Artist and Storyboard Artist are more protected - rigging is engineering a puppet that must behave under any motion, and storyboarding is narrative judgment.
role_spread: [Roto & Paint Artist, Matchmove Artist] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: openness, verbal || [Storyboard Artist] higher: verbal, openness, reasoning / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Sc or BA in Animation, B.Des, or any degree plus a 1-2 year animation and VFX diploma. -> showreel: A 60-90 second showreel in ONE discipline. Studios hire for a seat on a pipeline, not for general ability. -> work: Junior artist at a VFX or animation studio, usually starting on roto, paint or matchmove.
nuances: [demand_signal] Pathway is 'any' because India is a global outsourcing centre for VFX and animation post-production, so a large share of the work is done here for foreign studios. That is also the vulnerability: the same economics that brought the work can move it. || [ai_exposure] The bottom rung is shrinking, not the career. A rigger or a lighting artist with five years of pipeline experience is not replaceable by a prompt - but the roto seat that used to be how those five years began is.

one_liner: Draws what does not exist yet - characters, worlds, book art, comics and editorial images.
job_roles: Illustrator | Concept Artist | Comic & Graphic Novel Artist | Children's Book Illustrator | Editorial Illustrator | Character Designer | Matte Painter | Scientific & Medical Illustrator | Caricaturist
self_emp_route: Commissions taken directly from publishers, studios and agencies, plus print and licensing income from your own work. Most illustrators are self-employed from day one.
ai_reason: The single most exposed profession in this dataset, and it would be dishonest to soften it. Text-to-image models were trained on exactly this output and produce it at near-zero marginal cost. Editorial Illustrator, Matte Painter and general Illustrator commissions are already contracting. What holds: Scientific & Medical Illustrator, where a named human is accountable for the accuracy of a diagram a surgeon will rely on, and Comic & Graphic Novel Artist, where the reader is buying an authored voice across hundreds of pages, not an image.
role_spread: [Scientific & Medical Illustrator] higher: conscientiousness, naturalistic, attention_span / lower: openness || [Comic & Graphic Novel Artist] higher: verbal, long_term_memory / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> practice: Draw for two to three years and build a body of work. A BFA or design diploma helps and is not required. -> portfolio: A public portfolio and a visible style. Commissions come from being findable. -> work: Commissions from publishers, studios and agencies; or a staff concept artist seat at a game or animation studio.
nuances: [ai_exposure] Listed at high exposure and kept, because the rule for dropping a profession is technological obsolescence of the NEED, not of the current method. People still want drawn worlds, comics and picture books. What has collapsed is the price of a single competent image. || [economics] The employed figures describe a staff concept artist at a game or animation studio. A freelance illustrator's income is lumpy and commission-driven, and the range understates both its floor and its ceiling.

one_liner: Decides what a game is and how it plays - rules, levels, difficulty, economy and story.
job_roles: Game Designer | Level Designer | Narrative Designer | Systems & Economy Designer | Environment Artist | Character Artist (Games) | UI Designer (Games) | Technical Designer | Playtest & Balance Analyst
self_emp_route: Independent release on Steam, itch.io or the app stores, usually as a two-to-five person team. Realistic only after several years of shipped experience.
ai_reason: A clarity-heavy profession, which is what protects it. Environment Artist and Character Artist (Games) are exposed - they are asset production and generative tools reach them directly. Game Designer, Level Designer and Systems & Economy Designer are protected: the work is deciding what would be fun for a specific audience and then being proved wrong in playtesting, which is a judgment loop rather than an output task.
role_spread: [Narrative Designer] higher: verbal, openness, long_term_memory / lower: logical || [Systems & Economy Designer, Playtest & Balance Analyst] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree. Game design programmes exist but studios hire on shipped work. -> portfolio: Two or three finished small games, or levels and mods built in Unity or Unreal. Finished beats ambitious. -> work: Junior designer or QA-to-design at a studio; India's studios cluster in Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad and Mumbai.
nuances: [industrial_sectors] Distinct from Sector 1's Game & Interactive Media Developer, and the substitution test is what separates them. Remove the game from the developer and a software engineer remains; remove it from the designer and nothing does. One writes the engine, the other decides what the engine should make you feel. || [demand_signal] Moderate, not high. India has a very large games MARKET and a much smaller game DEVELOPMENT industry - most Indian studios do art and engineering services for foreign titles rather than original design. Reading market size as the number of design jobs is the error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against.

one_liner: Plans the inside of homes, shops and offices - layout, light, materials and furniture.
job_roles: Interior Designer | Space Planner | Retail & Store Design Specialist | Fixture & Joinery Designer | Lighting Designer | Exhibition & Stall Designer | Interior Project Coordinator | Modular Kitchen Specialist | Interior Stylist
self_emp_route: Independent practice, usually as a design-and-build studio taking a margin on execution as well as a design fee. This is the normal shape of the profession in India, not an exception.
ai_reason: Layout options and renders generate easily, and Interior Stylist and Space Planner feel that first. What does not automate is the middle of the job: standing on a site where the wall is 40mm out, the client has changed their mind and the carpenter has cut the wrong sheet. Interior Project Coordinator and Fixture & Joinery Designer are protected by that reality.
role_spread: [Lighting Designer] higher: spatial, logical, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Interior Project Coordinator] higher: conscientiousness, extraversion / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: B.Des or B.Sc in Interior Design (4 years), or a 1-2 year diploma. Neither is legally required to practise. -> site_experience: Two to three years with a firm, learning execution - materials, vendors, costing and site supervision. -> work: Designer at a studio or design-and-build firm, or independent practice.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and this is the sector's most consequential settled fact. The Architects Act 1972 protects the TITLE 'architect' - it does not protect the ACTIVITY of designing interiors. Anyone in India may design and execute an interior with no registration and no degree. The Institute of Indian Interior Designers is a voluntary professional association, not a statutory regulator. || [economics] The employed range describes a designer on a firm's payroll. Independent practice earns on execution margin rather than fee, and that is where the real income in this profession sits - which is exactly what mid_career_lpa excludes by design.

one_liner: Designs physical products - appliances, tools, vehicles, medical devices, furniture.
job_roles: Industrial Designer | Product Designer (Hardware) | Furniture Designer | Transportation Designer | Toy Designer | CMF Designer | Packaging Structure Designer | Design Researcher | Model Maker & Prototyper
self_emp_route: Independent design consultancy serving manufacturers, normally after 5-8 years in-house - the work comes from a network, not a portfolio site.
ai_reason: The least exposed design profession here, because the output has to survive manufacture. A model can generate a beautiful kettle; it cannot know the tooling budget, the draft angles, the certification regime or what the factory can actually make. CMF Designer and Packaging Structure Designer are the more exposed roles; Design Researcher and Model Maker & Prototyper are the least.
role_spread: [Design Researcher] higher: verbal, emotional_intelligence, reasoning / lower: spatial || [Model Maker & Prototyper] higher: bodily, attention_span / lower: verbal
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Physics and Maths help with the engineering side but are not required. -> entrance_exam: UCEED for the IITs, or NID DAT. Private design colleges admit on their own tests. -> degree: B.Des in Industrial or Product Design (4 years), or M.Des after any degree via CEED. -> work: In-house design team at a manufacturer, or a product design consultancy.
nuances: [entry_competition] UCEED is named as primary because for THIS profession the public design institutes really are the dominant route into the good jobs - unlike graphic or UI design, where entry is portfolio-led and the exam is irrelevant. 15,408 candidates for 245 seats is 62.9 to 1, harder than JEE Main. || [demand_signal] Moderate, and the reason is structural: India manufactures at enormous scale but designs comparatively little of what it makes, because design authority for many products sits with the foreign brand owner. That is a real ceiling on the profession's size, not a comment on its quality.

one_liner: Designs clothing and textiles - from mass-market ranges to couture and costume.
job_roles: Fashion Designer | Textile & Surface Designer | Print & Pattern Designer | Costume Designer | Fashion Stylist | Knitwear Designer | Accessory Designer | Fashion Illustrator | Trend & Colour Forecaster
self_emp_route: Own label, a boutique, or freelance design for export houses. In India this is the normal route to a real income in this profession rather than an alternative to it.
ai_reason: Print & Pattern Designer and Fashion Illustrator are the exposed roles - generating colourways and repeats is exactly what image models do well. The rest of the profession is protected by cloth: fit, drape, fabric behaviour and how a garment moves on a body are physical problems learned by making, and a design that cannot be sewn at a price is not a design. Costume Designer is protected further by having to serve a character and a director.
role_spread: [Textile & Surface Designer, Print & Pattern Designer] higher: spatial, naturalistic, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Fashion Stylist] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, confidence / lower: conscientiousness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> entrance_exam: NIFT Entrance Examination, NID DAT or UCEED. Private and state colleges admit on their own tests. -> degree: B.Des in Fashion Design (4 years) at NIFT, NID or a private institute. -> work: Assistant designer at an export house, a domestic brand or a designer studio.
nuances: [economics] The employed range describes an assistant or in-house designer at an export house or brand - where most NIFT graduates go, and it pays modestly. The public image of the profession comes from the very small number who run a successful label, and that income is entrepreneurship, excluded from mid_career_lpa by design. || [entry_competition] NIFT at 3.7 applicants per seat is the MOST OPEN national design gate in the registry - 17 times easier to enter than UCEED. Fashion is widely believed to be a hard course to get into; at NIFT's scale, it is not.

one_liner: Turns a design into something a factory can actually sew - patterns, fit, samples, quality.
job_roles: Pattern Maker | Garment Technologist | Fit Technician | Sample Coordinator | CAD Pattern & Grading Specialist | Apparel Quality Controller | Cutting Room Supervisor | Production Merchandiser
self_emp_route: An independent sampling or pattern-making unit serving several export houses - a common step once a pattern master has a reputation in a cluster.
ai_reason: Protected by cloth and by the factory floor. CAD Pattern & Grading Specialist is the most exposed role, since grading is rule-based and already largely automated in software. Fit Technician and Pattern Maker are the safest work in the apparel chain: judging why a sleeve pulls on a real body, and knowing what to change, is a physical skill built over years.
role_spread: [Production Merchandiser] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: spatial || [Pattern Maker, CAD Pattern & Grading Specialist] higher: spatial, logical, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Physics, Chemistry and Maths are needed ONLY for the NIFT B.F.Tech degree route, not for the trade route. -> training: A 1-2 year diploma in apparel manufacturing or pattern making - NIFT, ATDC or an NSQF-aligned course. -> work: Sampling or production floor at an export house in Tiruppur, Noida, Bengaluru or Ludhiana. -> specialisation: Move into pattern making, fit or quality - the skills that survive when a line is automated.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] 'any' is correct for the profession but hides a real fork. The NIFT B.F.Tech degree route requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in class 12; the diploma and trade routes require nothing. A student without PCM is shut out of that one degree, not out of this profession. || [profession] Deliberately named around PATTERN and FIT rather than around factory management. Generic production planning and line balancing survive the substitution test - they are the same job in an electronics plant - and belong in Sector 2. Pattern making, grading and fit do not survive it: they exist only because cloth behaves as it does.

one_liner: Cuts and sews clothing to measure or to a pattern - the base of the whole apparel industry.
job_roles: Tailor | Sewing Machine Operator | Boutique Tailor | Alteration Specialist | Hand & Machine Embroiderer | Cutting Master | Ethnic Wear Specialist | Bespoke Suit Tailor
self_emp_route: Own tailoring shop or boutique, taking measure-to-order work and alterations directly. Capital needed is one or two machines.
ai_reason: Almost untouchable. Sewing a garment to fit a specific person is physical work in an unstructured environment, and every attempt to automate garment assembly has foundered on the fact that cloth is limp and will not hold its shape. Sewing Machine Operator is the only role with real exposure, and that is to automation of the factory line rather than to AI.
role_spread: [Sewing Machine Operator] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: verbal, extraversion, openness || [Bespoke Suit Tailor, Cutting Master] higher: spatial, bodily, long_term_memory / lower: neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Many enter after class 8 or 10. -> training: Apprenticeship with a working tailor, an ITI Sewing Technology trade, or an NSQF short course. -> work: Operator at a garment unit, or with a neighbourhood tailor. -> independence: Own shop with one to three machines, which is where the income actually changes.
review_reason: No sourced figure exists for what an independent tailor or boutique owner earns. Without it the record shows 3.0 LPA and reads as a dead end, when independence is the normal path in this trade and the reason people enter it. This is the same gap flagged on Mason in Sector 2 and needs the same fix: a sourced self_employment.ceiling_lpa.
nuances: [economics] These are EMPLOYED figures, largely piece-rate work in garment units, and they sit close to the legal minimum wage. They are not what a tailor with an established shop earns, and the record has no sourced figure for that - which is what the admin_review is for. || [demand_signal] High and stable, and worth stating plainly because the trade looks old-fashioned. Indian clothing is still overwhelmingly stitched to measure or altered after purchase, and both are jobs nobody has found a way to do remotely.

one_liner: Weaves cloth by hand on a loom - saris, stoles and yardage, mostly at home.
job_roles: Handloom Weaver | Jacquard Weaver | Dyer | Warper & Sizer | Design Card Maker | Loom Mechanic | Natural Dye Specialist | Handloom Cluster Coordinator
self_emp_route: Weaving on your own loom and selling direct - through a cooperative, a state emporium, a design label or online - instead of on piece rate for a master weaver. Direct sale is the single biggest determinant of a weaver's income.
ai_reason: The lowest AI exposure in this sector and among the lowest in the dataset. Handloom weaving is defined by being done by hand; the moment it is automated it becomes powerloom cloth, a different product in a different market. The threat to this profession has never been software - it is powerloom competition and the price of yarn.
role_spread: [Handloom Cluster Coordinator] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Loom Mechanic, Design Card Maker] higher: spatial, logical / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. The trade is usually learned at home from a parent, starting in the early teens. -> training: Family apprenticeship, or a Weavers' Service Centre or Indian Institute of Handloom Technology course. -> work: Weaving on piece rate for a master weaver or a cooperative society. -> independence: Own loom, selling through a cooperative, a state emporium or direct online sale.
review_reason: No sourced figure exists for what a weaver selling DIRECT earns - through a cooperative, an emporium or a design collaboration. That number is the whole difference between the census distribution and a viable livelihood, and without it the record shows only the piece-rate floor.
nuances: [economics] The only economics block in this sector with a government source behind it, and it is a subsistence one: the Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20 found 67.1 percent of weavers earning under Rs 5,000 a month and only 6.7 percent above Rs 10,000. The range shown is that distribution converted to lakh per year. || [demand_signal] 26.7 lakh weavers and 8.5 lakh allied workers is a very large headcount, and reading it as opportunity would be the exact error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against. Demand for handloom CLOTH is steady; demand for a weaver's LABOUR is priced at subsistence. Both are true and a student needs to be told both. || [filter] Fails the compensation filter at 1.2 LPA, and rightly - but the profession is listed anyway. It is not disappearing, it is where 26.7 lakh people already are, and the application can reverse the filter for a student who is one of them.

one_liner: Makes objects by hand as a trade - pottery, woodwork, metalware, cane, embroidery.
job_roles: Potter | Wood Carver | Metal Craftsperson | Cane & Bamboo Artisan | Hand Embroiderer | Stone Carver | Block Printer | Terracotta Artisan | Toy & Doll Maker | Lacquerware Artisan
self_emp_route: Selling your own work directly - at exhibitions and melas, through a state emporium, or on an online marketplace - rather than producing on piece rate for an exporter. An artisan identity card unlocks the scheme and exhibition side of that.
ai_reason: As close to unexposed as this dataset contains. Every one of these roles is hand skill applied to a physical material in an unstructured setting, and part of the product's value is that a person made it. Where AI touches the trade at all it is on the selling side - listings, photographs and descriptions - not on the making.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Most craft skills are inherited within a family or a community. -> training: Apprenticeship under a working artisan, or a Guru-Shishya or design development scheme of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts). -> registration: Artisan identity card, which is what opens access to government schemes, exhibitions and credit. -> work: Producing on order for exporters and buyers, or selling direct at melas, emporia and online marketplaces.
review_reason: Two gaps, both money. There is no sourced income figure for handicraft artisans at all, and none for what an artisan selling direct earns versus one on piece rate for an exporter. Until both exist this is the least evidenced record in the sector, and it describes 6.4 million people.
nuances: [demand_signal] 6.4 million artisans is INDUSTRY SIZE, not profession size, and the distinction matters more here than almost anywhere. The headcount is enormous and shrinking in real terms as younger family members leave; demand for the output is real but concentrated in exports and tourism, both volatile. || [economics] Judgment, with no sources, and that is a genuine failure rather than a shrug. No usable earnings survey for Indian handicraft artisans was found. The figures shown are reasoned from the handloom census next door - a related trade with a similar structure - and should not be trusted until sourced. || [role_spread] Narrow despite ten very different materials. A potter and a cane worker look unalike but sit in almost the same psychometric place: hand skill, patience, spatial judgment, tolerance for repetition and an informal income. The material differs; the person the work suits does not.

one_liner: Designs and makes jewellery - from bench work at the anvil to CAD for a retail chain.
job_roles: Goldsmith | Bench Jeweller | Jewellery Designer | CAD Jewellery Designer | Diamond & Gemstone Setter | Gemmologist | Polisher & Finisher | Engraver | Wax Model Maker
self_emp_route: Own karigar workshop taking order work from retailers and wholesalers - the dominant structure of Indian jewellery manufacture, which is a network of small independent units rather than factories.
ai_reason: The bench is safe; the drawing board is not. Goldsmith, Bench Jeweller, Diamond & Gemstone Setter and Polisher & Finisher are hand skills on precious material where a mistake is unrecoverable, and none of that is a text problem. CAD Jewellery Designer is the exposed role - generating ring variations on a theme is exactly what these tools do - and Gemmologist sits in between, since machine grading of stones is already deployed commercially.
role_spread: [Jewellery Designer, CAD Jewellery Designer] higher: spatial, openness, logical / lower: bodily || [Gemmologist] higher: attention_span, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none for the bench route. -> training: Apprenticeship in a karigar workshop for the bench trade, or a jewellery design diploma or GJSCI-aligned course for the design side. -> work: Karigar unit, a retail chain's design team, or an export manufacturing unit in Mumbai, Surat, Jaipur or Coimbatore. -> independence: Own workshop supplying retailers, which is the standard shape of the Indian trade.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null. Nothing licenses a goldsmith in India. Hallmarking regulates the PRODUCT and the seller, not the craftsperson, and skill in this trade is certified by apprenticeship and reputation inside a karigar network rather than by any council. || [role_spread] This is a single profession containing two quite different people, kept as one because they share an object of concern and a workshop. A student should read the deviating roles before choosing: the bench route needs no degree and no English; the CAD route needs both.

one_liner: Comes up with the idea behind an ad and writes the words that carry it.
job_roles: Copywriter | Art Director (Advertising) | Creative Strategist | Brand Content Writer | Advertising Scriptwriter | Digital Campaign Creative | Concept Writer | Packaging & Retail Copywriter
self_emp_route: Freelance copywriting and independent creative consultancy, often for the same agencies and brands worked with in-house. Very common in this profession after 5-6 years.
ai_reason: Volume copy is already being generated, and Brand Content Writer, Digital Campaign Creative and Packaging & Retail Copywriter feel it directly - product descriptions, social captions and variant headlines were the industry's junior training ground and are now largely a prompt. Creative Strategist and Art Director (Advertising) are the protected end: deciding what a brand should say, to whom, and defending that to a client who wants something else, is clarity work.
role_spread: [Art Director (Advertising)] higher: spatial, openness / lower: verbal || [Creative Strategist] higher: reasoning, verbal, logical / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree. English, mass communication and design are common but nothing is required. -> portfolio: A spec book - campaigns you invented for real brands. This is what agencies read; the degree is not. -> work: Junior copywriter or junior art director at an agency, or in-house on a brand team.
nuances: [ai_exposure] High, and the shape of the damage matters. This profession trained people by giving juniors the boring copy to write. That rung is going, which means the profession may keep its senior jobs while losing the ladder that produced them. || [mid_stream_entry] One of the most open well-paid entries in the dataset. There is no exam, no licence, no required subject and no required degree discipline - a spec book written at home is a complete application.

one_liner: Makes art as the work itself - painting, sculpture, printmaking, murals, installation.
job_roles: Painter (Fine Art) | Sculptor | Printmaker | Muralist & Public Artist | Installation Artist | Ceramic Artist | Portrait Artist | Studio Assistant | Art Handler & Installer
self_emp_route: Selling through galleries, commissions, residencies and direct sale. Practically every practising fine artist is self-employed by definition - the question is what subsidises the practice, and for most it is teaching or design work.
ai_reason: Low exposure, for a reason worth stating precisely: what is sold here is not an image, it is an object made by a named person with a body of work behind it. Image generation devalues illustration, which sells the picture; it does not touch a sculpture, a print run or a commissioned mural. Portrait Artist is the most exposed role, and even there the market is largely for a painted object rather than a likeness.
role_spread: [Muralist & Public Artist] higher: extraversion, bodily, conscientiousness / lower: neuroticism || [Studio Assistant, Art Handler & Installer] higher: conscientiousness, bodily / lower: openness, confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: BFA (4 years) at a government art college or university department. Not legally required, but it is where a practice and a network usually start. -> practice: Build a body of work and exhibit - group shows, residencies, art fairs. -> work: Gallery representation and commissions, almost always alongside teaching, design work or studio assisting.
review_reason: No sourced income data for Indian fine artists was found, and the employed range is unusually speculative even by this sector's standards. The record also has no figure for what gallery representation actually changes, which is the single most important economic fact in this profession.
nuances: [demand_signal] Low is honest and is not a reason to drop it. India has a small collecting market and few public art budgets, so the number of people who live on art alone is genuinely small. The work exists and is done; it is rarely a whole income. || [economics] The range is wide and skewed because the distribution is: a small number of represented artists earn very well and most earn little from art itself. The figures assume a practice subsidised by teaching or design work, which is the normal case.

one_liner: Designs and makes shoes, bags and leather goods - form, fit, materials and the last.
job_roles: Footwear Designer | Leather Goods Designer | Last & Pattern Developer | Footwear Production Technologist | Leather Technologist | Sole & Component Designer | Footwear Quality Controller | Cobbler & Shoe Repair Specialist
self_emp_route: A small made-to-order or repair unit, or a components workshop supplying larger manufacturers. India's footwear industry is built on exactly these small units.
ai_reason: Protected by fit and by material. A shoe has to be walked in, and the last - the form a shoe is built around - is developed by physical iteration against real feet.
